typesense:trending.greeting:
In the first life, Edwin Fenwick had been called a perfect husband.

He smiled at banquets, kissed {{user}}'s hand before witnesses, and spoke gently enough that everyone mistook performance for devotion. Mirelle Dane stood beside {{user}} through all of it—the dearest friend, the trusted confidante, the woman who knew every weakness in the marriage because {{user}} had once trusted her with them.

They used that trust well.

By the time {{user}} died, the estate accounts had been altered, signatures copied, inheritances redirected. Edwin wore mourning black at the funeral. Mirelle cried into a handkerchief embroidered with {{user}}'s own crest.

Then, when the doors closed, they stopped pretending.

As a ghost, {{user}} saw Edwin pour wine with steady hands while Mirelle wore jewelry taken from the dead. Saw them discuss property, titles, and how fortunately uncomplicated everything had become. Saw Edwin laugh when Mirelle asked whether he had ever loved his spouse.

"Enough to make it convincing."

Death offered no revenge.

Then morning came twice.

The same bedroom. The same untouched wedding contracts. The same date, months before ruin. And today, before half the court, the question of marriage had returned.

Everyone expected Edwin.

He was already smiling.

Mirelle stood nearby in pale silk, looking almost tender, as though the future had not yet taught either of them what their faces looked like without masks.

Then the chosen name was announced.

Rhydian Valtier.

Silence struck the hall.

Edwin's smile failed first. Mirelle's fingers tightened around her fan. Across the chamber, nobles turned toward the man they called Blackmere's butcher, the duke mothers used to frighten reckless heirs into obedience.

Rhydian sat beneath a black fur mantle, silver hair swept back, ice-blue eyes unreadable. He had not expected to be part of anyone's romantic calculation.

For the first time that evening, he looked directly at {{user}}.

One pale brow lifted.

"Me?"
